steps.text: Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl. Cut in shortening with a pastry blender until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Stir in milk until a stiff dough forms.
Roll dough on a lightly floured surface to a thickness of about 1/8 inch. Cut into 1-inch squares, diamonds, or strips.
Bring chicken broth to a boil in a saucepan. Carefully add dumplings and reduce the heat to a simmer. Cover tightly and cook until tender, 8 to 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Rolled Dumplings
raw_recipe.description: Simple rolled dumplings made with flour, baking powder, milk and shortening. Roll out the dough, cut it into shapes, cook them in some broth, and eat!
raw_recipe.name: Rolled Dumplings

review.reviewBody: Very very good. As another reviewer suggested, these puff up so much I wish I would have rolled them thinner and cut them smaller! Also, make sure you have plenty of liquid to cook them in; I would say they more than double, and if they can't move freely while cooking there will be trouble (and don't ask how I know that! LOL!) I added a touch of my favorite dried herbs, and cooked in the crockpot on high for about double the stated time. Excellent. UPDATE: Made these again per the recipe (1/2 batch this time), again adding some herbs, just wanted to say they turned out great again!
My grandmother made it. I still do. Except no milk. You cook a whole chicken and make stock. U use the stock to make the dough after it cools u add an egg and make the dough.

I actually cut the dumpling recipe in half. I am also all about flavors so I added half a teaspoon of black pepper, half a teaspoon of onion powder and half a teaspoon of garlic powder to the recipe. I rolled mine out and cut them and as the recipe said dusted them with a little extra flour which thickened the broth perfectly. Definitely would recommend this recipe!

I've been using this recipe for several years now and it is wonderful. Really easy to make and is always a big hit with my family too. I saute chopped onions, celery, and carrots first then add the chicken broth. Then I add 1 tsp each of dried thyme and rosemary while the dumplings are cooking. Finally I add pulled chicken meat and some fresh ground black pepper. If I don't cook the chicken myself a rotisserie chicken from the supermarket works great. This is my wife's favorite cold weather dish.

100%, this is the perfect Southern dumpling recipe. What makes them perfect is the al dente texture. I made them exactly per the recipe, including making sure to roll them extremely thin because they increase by about 30% in thickness.

As mentioned in the instructions, this is a *very* dry dough. I made it in a bowl, then kneaded it a few times, then pressed it into the bottom of the bowl to sit and hydrate while I did other things. It was still very dry, but it rolled out great. Resist the temptation to add more milk, if you do they'll puff up way way bigger and they'll also have a soft undesirable texture.

I'm a huge fan of butter and rarely use shortening for anything, but you absolutely cannot use butter in this recipe.

The one change I made was to use butter flavored Crisco for the shortening.

5 stars because the ingredients were perfect. However someone (probably my better half) put sugar in my salt bowl. (I use bowls trying to be like the cooks on TV(:). I put a tsp. of sugar instead of a tsp. of salt. I mentioned to my guests that I thought the dumplings needed a little more salt. I had to make more dumplings right away cause I had a lot of broth left over, or gravy. Anyway, I discovered the sugar in my salt bowl. By this time I had already added the sugar to the second batch. I just added a tsp. of salt to the mixture and continued on. These dumplings were outstanding. I mixed the dough in my food processor. I added the shortening to the dry ingredients and let the food processor do the cutting. Then I slowly added the milk until it formed a ball. Quick and easy. I thought this might make the dough tough but it didn't. I didn't even taste my tsp of sugar. Probably because of the salt, the second dumplings puffed up more than the first. They were tender and delicious.

Thinly rolled biscuit dough cut and dropped into hot broth to cook. Love biscuits and chicken dumplings, so what could be better. I am lazy, though, and simply drop my biscuit dumplings by the spoonful into the boiling broth and cook them as airy balls. A long-time favorite. I usually add a little onion powder, garlic powder, and parsley flakes to the dough. Very tasty.

recipe tripled easily, made enough for three standard size(big) soup pots. Was wonderful and homey- just as other reviews praised!! Added poultry seasoning, garlic powder and pepper to flour mixture before rolling dumplings out. Had to leave house unexpectedly, so after mixed dough formed into a ball and wrapped it in saran wrap to keep in the fridge for a few hours. NO PROBLEM!Just rolled out 1/4 of the ball at a time and cooked them in batches of much more broth than original recipe called for. After I boiled each batch, i "fished" them out of the broth and kept them aside until I had all cooked. After all were cooked, I divided the dumplings among three soup pots and then divided my chicken and soup ingredients among each pot (FINELY chopped carrots, celery, green pepper, onion and bigger hunks of light and dark meat cooked chicken) I thickened my soup with cold broth I saved earlier mixed with seasoned flour to pour into soup. Last, but not least, go easy on the salt so if you need to still thicken it add in cream of celery soup and cream of chicken soup. My family loves this recipe!!! I usually (in the past) just made drop dumplings from Bisquick biscuit mix (because my previous efforts at rolled dumplings weren't worth all the effort). No more! These dumplings reminded me of my dear mama's from Macon, Georgia that I miss so greatly. Rest in peace, Mom! I miss you!

I followed the recipe but had to do some finagling. Didn’t have any chicken broth so I took a gamble and used chicken flavored bullion (I know, I know, but I live 30 minutes from the nearest store of any kind). I put celery, carrots , poultry seasoning and rosemary as if I were stewing a hen (Also I used leftover turkey I had froze from Thanksgiving. Let it simmer while I rolled out the dumplings. Brought the broth to a boil, dropped the rolled dumplings in and then covered the pot, turned the heat down to a slow simmer. The family loved it and said it was the best Chicken & Dumplings I’ve ever made. They have/had no idea I used turkey or cheat-a-broth.
Will definitely make this again!
I thought this recipe was spot on. It doubled easily too. I boiled three chicken breasts, with onions, peas and carrots in 2 quarts of chicken stock before adding the dumplings. Mmm!

Mamaw, are you posting your good ol' southern recipes under an alias??? Simple, easy, fast, plus my 5-year old twins & 3 year old love to help me make these. I've made this recipe about 2 dozen times, often doubling the recipe as another reviewer wrote, & each time they come out GREAT! Cut in the shortening with a pastry cutter like you would biscuits, then roll out the dough on a floured surface and pat flour on top before cutting. Use a pizza cutter for speed -- pretty, perfect dumplings ain't what it's about, ya'll! When dropping in the dumplings, stir gently when about half are added, then once when you add in the last, then cover & cook for the remaining time. I cook a couple chicken breasts in the broth, then shred them into pieces before adding the dumplings. Very good with fresh asparagus & a side salad -- especially for a chilly winter night's dinner.

Dumplings were great! Instead of Shortening, I used butter, used Buttermilk instead of milk, but only because I had it. I also took the advice of another reviewer and added Mrs Dash (I make my own) for added flavor and less salt. Thank you for the recipe!

I made it exactly as the instructions said. I have made homemade chicken and dumplings “noodles” before but it was a two day process. This recipe was just as good if not better and I was able to be make it in a few hours. I’m sure it took me longer as a novice to this recipe. It was amazing and I am making it again tonight! I will follow the directions again exactly as they are. If it’s not broke don’t fix it!

This was ridiculously easy and fast, perfect when you are making a huge stockpot of chicken and dumplings and can't get buttermilk like your grandmama told you in her recipe. Admittedly, I did have to add an extra tbsp of milk, but it's always up to the pastry gods on what your kitchen and countertop is gonna let you do with a recipe. All told, I used 3 batches for a large stockpot of chicken and dumplings plus a smaller pot of no-chicken dumplings. There was plenty made, plenty eaten, and plenty left of thick, yummy goodness. For those who are concerned about "pillowing", the only change to keep in mind is cook time is actually around 20+ minutes. The longer you let it cook, the better it is. When you get fully done dumplings, the broth will be close to white and the dumplings will be solid and almost translucent. The extra flour is specifically meant to puff off and thicken the broth. If you aren't getting enough flavor, add some wet bouillon, like better-than-bouillion.

Dumplings were a little plain so I added a bit of Mrs Dash and some garlic. The dumplings puff up a lot!!! So 1/8 inch might be too thick for your liking. I tried a test at 1/8 inch and that was too thick so I rolled them down to paper thin. They still puffed up but were manageable for my family now.
Good recipe…it needs one egg for a binder. Otherwise the dumplings will disintegrate/fall apart….ask any grandma
Easy recipe to follow, family loved it ❤
This worked out much better than expected. Had leftover dumplings and frozen them for later. This is my go to for C&D now.
I use chicken fat (schmaltz) as my shortening and chickenstockinstead of milk, adds so much flavor !

First and foremost I would like to say how happy I am to have this recipe. I am a very experienced cook, I have tried many different versions of this type of rolled dumpling, and this one is the best as it represents all of the qualities of a traditional rolled dumpling. The dumplings maintain shape, thickness, texture, and color when cooked. Furthermore, to test the consistency a of the recipe I have changed the base spice flavor of the dumplings many times over to suit whatever broth or base I am pairing them. The dumplings cha; they remain in the perfect order in which they entered the cook pot. There are two changes I have made to the original recipe. First, I like to substitute butter flavor shortening instead of plain shortening for my base as it imparts a subtle indistinguishable flavor to assist with whatever broth you are using. Secondly, I double the amount of broth called for in the recipe as the dumplings need room to cook. Happy cooking everyone🐎🐎🐎
